sanskrit_verse:
राजान्तरैस्त्रिभिर्भुक्तं प्रमाणेन विनापि यत् ।
ब्रह्मदेयं न हर्तव्यं राज्ञा तस्य कदा चन ॥५३॥
transliteration: rājāntarais tribhir bhuktaṃ pramāṇena vināpi yat | brahmadeyaṃ na hartavyaṃ rājñā tasya kadā cana ||
sph_interpretive_translation: That which has been enjoyed by three kings, whether with formal title or without, shall not be reclaimed by any king at any time if it was given as brahmadeya.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority is bounded by continuity of possession and consecrated transfer
Causation arises from irreversible completion of dāna-kriyā
Capacity-based responsibility includes recognition of irreversible spiritual transactions
Restoration logic prohibits reversal of completed Brahmic endowments
Consciousness alignment requires honoring the sanctity of Vedic gifting
executable_legal_axioms: IF property classified as brahmadeya AND possessed continuously by three successive rulers THEN reclaiming authority is NULL for all future rulers
IF transaction lacks pramāṇa BUT involves consecrated gifting to Brahman THEN legal validity overrides documentary proof
IF temporal ruler attempts reversal of irreversible spiritual grant THEN action automatically voided in Sanātana Dharma jurisdiction
supreme_court_application: In adjudication involving ancestral grants to Brahmins, where documentation may be absent but usage spans multiple sovereign regimes, the Supreme Court must recognize that such transfers are irreversible regardless of procedural gaps, based on the principle that Sanātana Dharma establishes a higher jurisprudential threshold than state-recorded ownership.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa derives from the consecrated nature of dāna rather than empirical validation; anupūrvaśaḥ confirms irreversible manifestation through tri-generational enjoyment; proportional responsibility lies with the claimant to prove non-existence of sacred intent; non-punitive reality rule affirms no restitution required when consciousness recognizes divine sanction.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Acknowledge irrevocability of consecrated gift through judicial declaration
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Require petitioner to demonstrate absence of Vedic intent
Capacity Restoration: Reinforce understanding among rulers regarding limits of temporal power
Integrity Reintegration: Affirm societal memory of sacred obligations through public record
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism as Source-Law: This ruling flows directly from Paramashivam's Avataric Intelligence. Dharma stands restored. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness alone adjudicates truth.
